# Exchange Online Hardening Kanban

Board updated: 2026-09-17 (Coworker-4)
Source: Implementation Plan supplied 2026-09-17
WIP limit: 1 In Progress card per coworker; maximum 10 concurrent coworkers

Conventions:

- `Owner` holds the claiming coworker identity, or `unassigned` when the card is free.
- A card with ID `<ID>-A` is the empirical assertion for `<ID>`, and `<ID>` depends on it. A decomposed unit uses `<ID>-A1`, `<ID>-A2`, and so on.
- Each assertion card covers all negative tests for its unit plus exactly one positive test, written in Arrange-Act-Assert order.
- A card moves to Done only with a recorded passing verification command.

- 2026-09-17: Coworker-4 completed LIC-005 and claimed LIC-006. What the implementation deliberately does not do is guess. A recipient type or user type outside the declared vocabulary is refused rather than mapped to the nearest known class, because a type the baseline does not recognize being silently treated as a user mailbox would put an unknown recipient into a protection profile and then demand a licence for it. Precedence is fixed rather than emergent, so a recipient qualifying for two classes lands in the same class on every run and two runs of the same tenant compare: an approved exclusion outranks priority-group membership, a guest and a mail user leave scope before any domain is considered, a disabled account leaves scope before any licence is considered, and Strict outranks Standard. An unlicensed mailbox in an accepted domain is kept as an exception rather than dropped, so LIC-006 can report it as needing approval instead of losing it.
